metaDescription: Four rolling plant caddies under $25 compared on wheel locks, load ratings from 240 to 450 lbs, round vs adjustable bases and what a bigger budget adds.
introParagraphs: A plant caddy is a small wheeled base that lets you slide a heavy pot across the floor instead of lifting it. At this budget the choice is shaped by three things: how much weight the base is rated for, whether the wheels lock, and whether the base fits the pot you actually own. Get any one of those wrong and a cheap caddy becomes a wobbly one.

We evaluated four distinct caddies that sit under this ceiling: a Bamworld 12 inch wood tray two pack, a Lissomballon 12 inch wood two pack rated for 240 lbs, a VANCASTLE adjustable 15 to 22 inch frame with a headline 450 lb rating, and a WanderingDonkey 14 inch plastic saucer style caddie rated for 265 lbs. Only four true models exist in this price band, so we did not pad the list.
Each is compared on size, capacity, wheel locks and what the listing leaves unsaid, with notes on what a larger budget would add.

products.name: Lissomballon 12 Inch Wood Plant Caddy, 2 Pack
products.description:
The Lissomballon is a round 12 inch wood caddy sold as a two pack, with a carbon wood frame and 360 degree lockable casters. The listing rates it for 240 lbs and says it fits pots from small succulent containers to large heavy planters. It also suggests uses beyond plants, such as laundry bins and trash cans.

The lockable casters are the headline advantage at this budget, because a pot that rolls when you want it to stay put is a real nuisance on a slope or a busy floor. A pair also lets you move two medium pots, or share the load of one wide planter. The wood frame gives a natural look indoors, but wood near standing water can swell, so use a saucer or drip tray on top of it.

In ownership, assembly is part of the deal, and the wheels need to be tightened properly. Against the WanderingDonkey at 14 inch and 265 lbs you get locking wheels and a second caddy but a smaller platform. Against the Bamworld two pack at the same 12 inch size, check the product pages for the difference in wheel and frame details, because the sizes match. Because it comes as a pair, you can also place one under a plant and keep the second as a spare for the next repot.
products.bestFor: Indoor plants of moderate weight where wheel locks matter.

products.name: Bamworld 12 Inch Plant Caddy, 2 Pack
products.description:
The Bamworld caddy is a 12 inch round wood tray with metal connections and casters that the listing says lock, sold as a two pack. It targets indoor pots and describes 360 degree rolling. The listing calls the wood premium and the movement smooth and reliable.

This pack suits a home with two or three pots of similar size, since the 12 inch platform matches many nursery pots and mid sized planters. The listing does not state a load rating, so check the product page before putting a large, watered planter on it. A wooden tray also looks more at home in a living room than a plastic saucer does.

In ownership, keep the wood dry and put a tray under the pot, because water on wooden trays can swell or stain them over time. Compared with the Lissomballon, which states 240 lbs, the Bamworld gives you the same size and pack count but a less specific capacity statement. For a guaranteed weight rating, the VANCASTLE and WanderingDonkey both state theirs. A pair also keeps the look consistent if you line two pots up along a wall.
products.bestFor: Living rooms with two or three medium pots.
cons: Load rating not given in the listing text

products.name: WanderingDonkey 14 Inch Plant Caddie
products.description:
The WanderingDonkey is a one piece plastic caddie with a 14.17 inch outer diameter and a 12.68 inch inner diameter, rated for 265 lbs. It arrives ready to use with no assembly, and the listing describes toughened tempered plastic and a frosted surface. It rolls on hardwood, concrete and carpet.

The saucer shape is a plus for people who want to catch a little water, and the plastic is fine on a patio. The listing does not mention wheel locks, which matters on a slope or a busy floor, and the saucer has no drain holes, so a plant with a draining pot can leave a puddle. It is the only pick here that skips assembly entirely.

In ownership, there is nothing to tighten or reattach, which suits anyone who has had wheels loosen on a cheaper unit. Against the Lissomballon at 240 lbs, it adds 25 lbs of rating and about two inches of platform, while giving up locking casters. Against the VANCASTLE, it is a fixed size, so it fits one range of pots instead of flexing to many.
products.bestFor: Heavier pots on a patio or hard floor, with no assembly.
pros: Ready to use with no assembly
265 lbs rating above the 240 lb pair
Rolls on hardwood, concrete and carpet
cons: No drain holes in the saucer

products.name: VANCASTLE Adjustable Plant Caddy, 15 to 22 Inch
products.description:
The VANCASTLE is not a fixed tray but an adjustable frame, with ABS panels and stainless steel tubes that expand from 15 to 22 inch. The listing says the wheels lock and claims a 450 lb capacity in the title, while one description line gives 440 lbs. We treat the capacity as roughly that range and suggest confirming it before loading.

The adjustable range is its biggest advantage. Where a 12 inch round caddy is too small for a wide ceramic planter, this frame covers up to 22 inch, which is a size cheaper caddies simply do not reach. The listing contrasts its wheel against a normal plastic single wheel and states the capacity is much higher.

In ownership, an adjustable frame needs setup and a check that all fasteners are tight and the load sits centered. Against the 12 inch Lissomballon and Bamworld, it reaches pots nearly twice as wide, and against the WanderingDonkey at 265 lbs it states much more capacity. You pay for that with a frame that has more parts that can loosen, so check it after the first week of use. Expand the frame to just under the pot base width, so the pot sits inside the corners instead of overhanging.
products.bestFor: Wide or heavy planters that fixed trays cannot fit.
cons: Capacity listed inconsistently at 450 and 440 lbs
More parts to tighten after setup

buyingCriteria.explanation: Check the rating against a fully watered pot with soil and plant, not an empty pot. A wet 14 inch ceramic planter can weigh far more than its size suggests, so give yourself a margin of at least 20 percent. In this lineup the Lissomballon is rated for 240 lbs, the WanderingDonkey for 265 lbs and the VANCASTLE for roughly 440 to 450 lbs. If you cannot lift the pot comfortably, treat the heavier ratings as the safer choice. As a worked example, a 12 inch pot holding about 30 lbs of wet soil and a 10 lb plant is a 40 lb load, which any pick here handles. A large 20 inch planter can pass 150 lbs once watered, and that is where the VANCASTLE becomes the only sensible option in this lineup.

Locking casters keep a pot from drifting on a slope, near a door or when you brush against it. At least two locking wheels is a practical minimum. The Lissomballon, Bamworld and VANCASTLE state locks, while the WanderingDonkey listing does not mention them. If you are placing a tall plant near a walkway, choose a locking model. Locks also help when you water in place, because a pot that shifts under a watering can splash onto the floor. Remember that a lock holds one wheel, so a caddy with a single locking caster can still pivot around it.

buyingCriteria.criterion: Match caddy size to pot base
buyingCriteria.explanation: The base of the pot should sit fully on the caddy, with room to spare for repotting. Round caddies under a square pot leave the corners unsupported. The Lissomballon and Bamworld are both 12 inch, the WanderingDonkey is 14.17 inch outside and 12.68 inch inside, and the VANCASTLE adjusts from 15 to 22 inch. Measure the pot base, not the rim. Leave about an inch of clearance around a round base, so the pot does not rock on its edge. The WanderingDonkey's 12.68 inch inner diameter is the number to compare against your pot base, since the outer 14.17 inch figure includes the rim.

Wood suits indoor use but can swell with standing water, while plastic and ABS resist moisture better on a patio. The Lissomballon and Bamworld are wood, the WanderingDonkey uses tempered plastic and the VANCASTLE uses ABS panels with steel tubes. Put a saucer under any wood caddy. For outdoor use, plastic or ABS is usually the easier choice. Outdoors, rain and sun hit wood fastest, so a patio caddy belongs in plastic or ABS. Indoors, wood is fine as long as you empty the saucer after watering.

Cheap caddies often fail where the wheel attaches, so tighten the casters fully and check them after a week. The WanderingDonkey needs no assembly and so has nothing to loosen. The Lissomballon and VANCASTLE need setup, and the VANCASTLE has the most parts. Plan five to ten minutes and a screwdriver. A quick test is to lift the caddy by its rim and rock a wheel, since a wheel that moves at the mount will fail first under load.

Spending more tends to buy more wheels, larger sizes and stronger frames. This price band tops out around 14 inch fixed trays and one adjustable frame. A step up reaches Bosmere models with a stated 500 lb capacity and 16 inch bases. If your heaviest pot is a concrete planter, that step is worth considering.

howWeEvaluated.title: Capacity and stated limits
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared stated load, from the Lissomballon at 240 lbs to the VANCASTLE near 450 lbs, and noted where listings give no rating, as the Bamworld does. We treated the VANCASTLE's 450 and 440 lb figures as a range. We did not assume a capacity where none was stated. We also weighed the gap between the lowest and highest rating, since 240 lbs versus roughly 450 lbs separates a medium houseplant from a large floor planter.

howWeEvaluated.title: Wheel and lock features
howWeEvaluated.description: Locks were weighed heavily because a rolling pot is a safety issue on slopes. The Lissomballon, Bamworld and VANCASTLE state locking wheels, while the WanderingDonkey does not. We also considered whether the wheels are 360 degree swivel casters. A caddy that cannot be locked was scored lower for slopes, entryways and kids or pets who may bump a pot.

howWeEvaluated.title: Fit and size range
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared platform sizes, from 12 inch round to the VANCASTLE's 15 to 22 inch range. A caddy that cannot fit the pot base is not usable no matter how well built. The WanderingDonkey sits in the middle at 14.17 inch outside. We checked the stated inner diameter where it was given, since the platform that holds the pot is smaller than the outer edge.

howWeEvaluated.title: Material and setup
howWeEvaluated.description: Wood, plastic and ABS each have indoor and outdoor tradeoffs. The WanderingDonkey needs no assembly, while the VANCASTLE has the most setup steps. We considered how likely each is to loosen over time.

howWeEvaluated.title: Value in this band
howWeEvaluated.description: Only four true models sit under the cap, so the comparison focuses on trade offs between a locking pair, an unlocked heavier caddie and an adjustable frame. Positioning comes from listing specs and buyer feedback, not hands on measurement.

howToChoose.intro: Do you want a tray that matches one pot or a frame that fits many?

cards.label: Fixed tray
cards.text: A tray such as the Lissomballon, Bamworld or WanderingDonkey is rigid and simple, with fewer parts to loosen. It works when your pots share a similar base size. Choose a tray if your pots are 12 to 14 inch.

cards.label: Adjustable frame
cards.text: The VANCASTLE expands from 15 to 22 inch with steel tubes, so it fits many pot sizes and shapes. It needs more setup and checking. Choose it if your pots vary or you own wide planters.

howToChoose.note: Adjustable frames suit square and rectangular pots better than round trays do.

faq.q: Which plant caddy under this budget is best?
faq.a: The Lissomballon two pack is the best value for medium pots because it states locking casters and a 240 lbs rating. The VANCASTLE is better for wide or heavy planters. The WanderingDonkey is best if you want no assembly. Choose the VANCASTLE only if you really need that size range, since its extra parts add maintenance.

faq.q: How much weight can these caddies hold?
faq.a: The Lissomballon is rated for 240 lbs, the WanderingDonkey for 265 lbs and the VANCASTLE for roughly 440 to 450 lbs. The Bamworld listing does not state a rating. Always include the soil and water weight in your estimate.

If you place a plant on a slope or near a doorway, yes. A pot that rolls can be a hazard and can tip. The WanderingDonkey listing does not mention locks, so avoid it for those spots. If you want a tall plant to stay where you set it, pick a model that states locks.

faq.q: Are wood caddies safe for indoor floors?
faq.a: They are fine if you keep water off them. Wood can swell with standing water, so put a saucer under the pot. Plastic and ABS caddies are easier to keep dry.

faq.q: Will a 12 inch caddy fit my pot?
faq.a: Only if the base of your pot is 12 inch or smaller. Measure the bottom of the pot, not the rim. Wider pots need the WanderingDonkey, which has a 12.68 inch inner diameter, or the VANCASTLE. Pots with flared rims often have a much smaller base, so a pot that looks 14 inch wide at the top may still fit a 12 inch caddy.

faq.q: Why does the VANCASTLE list two capacities?
faq.a: The listing states 450 lbs in the title and 440 pounds in one description line. We treat that as a range, and you should confirm the number before loading it near the top. For any weight close to the limit, buy a stronger caddy.

Buyers often report that wheels can loosen or detach under heavy use. Tighten the casters at setup and check them after the first week. Keep loads well below the rating. Smaller loads also let a wheel last longer, so a 40 lb pot on a 240 lb caddy will outlast a 200 lb pot on the same base.
